security_audit.summary: The confirmed issues are the intended RunComfy CLI execution path and the documented outbound API request to RunComfy. Most other static hits are Markdown backticks, documentation links, endpoint ellipses, or normal token-storage documentation, and no prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution is required for image generation.
remediation.suggestion: Ask users for confirmation before installing or running RunComfy commands, and show the exact command before execution.

remediation.issue: User prompts and bearer tokens are sent to RunComfy endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly disclose third-party processing, avoid sending sensitive prompt content, and document token revocation steps.

remediation.issue: Generated files are downloaded to a user-selected output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated output directory, preserve the download host whitelist, and keep the documented file-size cap.

content.user_title: Generate Fast Flux 2 Klein Images on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Fast image iteration is hard when prompts, variants, and reference images are unclear. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical RunComfy guidance for Flux 2 Klein generation.
actual_capabilities: Selects the 4B variant for rapid concepting and the 9B variant for polished output.
Provides RunComfy CLI invocation patterns for text-to-image generation.
Explains prompt structure that works well with Flux 2 Klein.
Documents width, height, step count, and reference-image constraints.
Summarizes RunComfy polling, output downloads, and common exit codes.
Advises when another image model may fit better than Flux 2 Klein.
limitations: Requires a working RunComfy account and local RunComfy CLI setup.
Sends prompts and supported reference inputs to RunComfy for processing.
Does not provide self-hosted Flux inference or local model weights.
Is not optimized for 4K output, extreme aspect ratios, or heavy in-image text.

use_cases.title: Rapid Concept Exploration
use_cases.description: Use the 4B variant to test visual directions quickly before committing to a final render.

use_cases.title: Product Image Drafting
use_cases.description: Generate product-style images with specific lighting, composition, lens, and surface details.

use_cases.title: Brand Style Alignment
use_cases.description: Use aligned reference images to keep asset packs visually consistent across a campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Image Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one simple image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Flux 2 Klein prompt for a clean product image of a ceramic mug on a neutral table.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Variant
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request where speed and quality tradeoffs matter.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose Flux 2 Klein 4B or 9B for a fast product concept session, then write the prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Reference Image Direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow with style or composition references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Flux 2 Klein prompt that keeps the reference composition but changes the background to a studio scene.

prompt_templates.title: Full RunComfy Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that needs command planning and output handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Flux 2 Klein RunComfy generation workflow with variant choice, prompt, dimensions, steps, and output directory guidance.

output_examples.input: I need fast ideas for a campaign hero image with a reusable brand style.
output_examples.output: Use Flux 2 Klein 4B for exploration, keep reference images visually aligned, and move the best prompt to 9B for final polish.

output_examples.input: My prompt includes a label with small text and a very wide banner layout.
output_examples.output: Reduce the aspect ratio, keep text short and high contrast, and consider GPT Image 2 if exact typography is required.

output_examples.input: I want a polished product render after several quick drafts.
output_examples.output: Start with a concise subject-first prompt, then use the 9B variant with a moderate step count for detail and texture.

best_practices: Start prompts with the subject, then add action, scene, style, lighting, camera, and quality details.
Use 4B for quick exploration and 9B when the composition is ready for polish.
Keep reference images visually consistent so style guidance does not conflict.
anti_patterns: Do not ask Flux 2 Klein for 4K native output or extreme aspect ratios.
Do not mix unrelated reference styles in one generation request.
Do not send sensitive or private content unless third-party RunComfy processing is acceptable.

faq.question: Does this skill run Flux 2 Klein locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to call the RunComfy hosted Model API.

faq.question: Which Flux 2 Klein variant should I use first?
faq.answer: Use 4B for quick concepting and 9B for higher fidelity final outputs.

faq.question: Can it use reference images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains reference-image use and recommends keeping references visually aligned.

faq.question: Is it good for text inside images?
faq.answer: It can handle simple text better with clear prompts, but exact typography may require a different image model.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI, authenticate with RunComfy, and choose an output directory for generated files.

faq.question: Does it send my prompt to a third party?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and supported inputs are sent to RunComfy because the model runs through the RunComfy API.
